summary.title: Full Stack Web Application using React, Node.js, Express and Webpack
summary.one_liner: You learn how to hand-configure a full stack React + Express project with Babel, ESLint (Airbnb rules), Prettier, Webpack, nodemon and concurrently, as an alternative to Create React App.
takeaways: Create React App hides its build config, which makes it hard to extend and to integrate with an existing Express backend.
In development, webpack-dev-server serves the React client with hot reloading while nodemon restarts the Express server; in production, Express serves the bundled static files.
Babel (preset-env and preset-react) transpiles modern JavaScript and JSX; webpack bundles client code with loaders and plugins.
ESLint with Airbnb's style guide and Prettier are configured for both browser and Node code, with VSCode auto-fix on save.
summary.summary: The article walks through setting up a simple full stack app with a React client and an Express API backend, explaining each config file in turn. It covers .babelrc, the ESLint config (Airbnb style guide, with some rules turned off), a webpack.config.js with babel and CSS loaders, the devServer proxy to /api, and a nodemon config watching src/server. It also shows how concurrently runs both servers in dev, and how Express serves the bundled dist folder in production. The guide ends with a VSCode + ESLint + Prettier setup. The example project is a small endpoint that returns the OS username.
